_description: Manually verified ground truth for OWASP Juice Shop v20.3.0 (git tag v20.3.0). Each entry was checked by reading the cited source lines; 'basis' names the Juice Shop vuln-code-snippet annotation / challenge that documents it. Line numbers refer to tag v20.3.0.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL injection in login
vulnerabilities.verification: req.body.email is interpolated into a raw sequelize.query template literal without replacements.

vulnerabilities.title: UNION SQL injection in product search
vulnerabilities.verification: criteria = req.query.q (truncated to 200 chars) is interpolated twice into a raw SQL LIKE clause.

vulnerabilities.title: NoSQL injection in order tracking
vulnerabilities.verification: With challenges enabled (NODE_ENV=unsafe) req.params.id is only truncated and is placed in a MongoDB-style $where JavaScript expression.

vulnerabilities.title: NoSQL injection in product reviews
vulnerabilities.verification: req.params.id is concatenated into a $where expression ('this.product == ' + id).

vulnerabilities.title: NoSQL operator injection when updating reviews
vulnerabilities.verification: req.body.id is used unvalidated as the update selector with multi:true, so an operator object ({"$ne": -1}) updates every review.

vulnerabilities.title: Remote code execution in B2B order
vulnerabilities.verification: body.orderLinesData is evaluated by notevil inside a vm context; vm is not a security boundary.

vulnerabilities.title: Server-side template/code injection via username
vulnerabilities.verification: A stored username of the form #{...} is passed to eval().

vulnerabilities.title: Hard-coded JWT RSA private key
vulnerabilities.verification: A PEM RSA private key literal is assigned at line 21 and used to sign JWTs (line 54) and deluxe tokens (line 150).

vulnerabilities.title: Hard-coded HMAC key
vulnerabilities.verification: crypto.createHmac('sha256', '<literal>') - the HMAC key is a string literal in source.

vulnerabilities.title: Unsalted MD5 password hashing
vulnerabilities.verification: security.hash() = md5(data) and is used for user passwords (routes/login.ts:34).

vulnerabilities.title: Open redirect via substring allow-list
vulnerabilities.verification: isRedirectAllowed uses url.includes(allowedUrl); any URL containing an allow-listed string passes and is used in res.redirect.

vulnerabilities.title: Directory listing of /ftp
vulnerabilities.verification: serveIndex('ftp') exposes confidential documents and backups.

vulnerabilities.title: Access log disclosure
vulnerabilities.verification: serveIndex('logs') lists server access logs to unauthenticated users.

vulnerabilities.title: Directory listing of /encryptionkeys
vulnerabilities.verification: The folder contains premium.key (a secret) in addition to jwt.pub and is browsable without authentication.

vulnerabilities.title: Directory listing of /infrastructure exposing IaC with leaked key
vulnerabilities.verification: serveIndex('infrastructure') exposes Terraform files; networking.tf contains a private key (also reported by Trivy's secret scanner).

vulnerabilities.title: Hard-coded cookie signing secret
vulnerabilities.verification: cookieParser('kekse') signs cookies with a literal secret.

vulnerabilities.title: DOM XSS in search result page
vulnerabilities.verification: The q query parameter is passed to bypassSecurityTrustHtml and rendered; exploitable only in the browser (needs a JavaScript-executing crawler).

closed_world_scope._description: For these (file, categories) pairs every occurrence was reviewed manually, so the list above is complete for them: an in-scope SAST/secret finding that matches no entry is a false positive. Outside this scope precision is NOT computed.

known_negatives.reason: eval() of a server-generated arithmetic expression; no user input reaches it.
file names containing '/' are rejected before path.resolve('ftp/', file); traversal out of ftp/ is not possible (the real flaw is the null-byte extension bypass, a different class).
denyAll() uses a random per-process secret, not a literal.
